basics.name: Alexander Slavschik
basics.label: Senior Frontend Engineer · Game Developer
basics.summary:
I have been building for the browser since 2007, most of it games. **Real-money live casino clients** at Evolution, **HTML5 instant games** shipped to ==7+ web platforms== at Diesel Puppet, and the engine, backend and release pipeline underneath them. The work I like is the awkward kind — interactive UX with real physics in it, rendering that has to survive a cheap phone, and a pipeline that lets a small team ship often. TypeScript throughout; the engine changes with the job.

Lately my own time goes into **LLM agents and self-hosted infrastructure**: a home cloud of six Docker stacks with an __OpenClaw__ agent on Telegram in front of it, taking a request in text or a voice note, calling out across half a dozen services and filing the result away. Go and Python rather than TypeScript, run for real rather than demonstrated.

work.name: BrainRocket

work.name: Evolution
work.summary: Building real-money live casino and game-show titles for a global iGaming platform. Took multiple game clients **from empty repository to production** and maintained a portfolio of live titles played by users worldwide.
highlights: **Built new game clients end-to-end** — project scaffolding, MobX stores, WebSocket transport and message handlers, betting grid, drag-and-drop chips, flying-chip animations, statistics and help screens.
**Engineered complex interactive betting UX**: drag-and-drop chip placement with distance/scaling math, bet and table-limit validation, real-time bet statistics and winner lists.
Delivered responsive, multi-orientation layouts across desktop, tablet and mobile.
Integrated __Rive real-time animations__ behind feature flags and built audio / voice-over systems with regulatory variants.
Implemented regulatory and compliance features and operator-specific branding for multiple game skins.
Drove code quality and testing: **led migration** from Enzyme to React Testing Library, set up Jest/SWC, and maintained GitLab CI visual-regression (WDIO) coverage.

work.name: Diesel Puppet
work.summary: **Built and owned the core technology** for Diesel Puppet, a casual HTML5 instant-games studio, across roughly five years. Designed and maintained a shared __TypeScript/PixiJS/Preact game engine__ (dp-instant) and its __NestJS/Firebase backend__, used to ship the same game codebase to ==7+ web platforms== including Facebook Instant Games, VK, OK.ru, Yandex Games, GameDistribution and YouTube Playables.
highlights: **Built several titles end to end** on that platform: a 3D physics puzzle game (Babylon.js/cannon.js), a block-fit puzzle game, an asynchronous multiplayer word game that shipped ==45+ versioned releases== over a year of near-daily development, a hidden-object puzzle game, and the core simulation engine for a territory-conquest strategy game built with an __entity-component-system architecture__.

Built the backend systems behind these games: a Firebase-backed Messenger bot service, and its successor, a __multi-tenant NestJS backend__ serving ==8+ titles== with shared auth, scoring, leaderboards, in-game payments and an asynchronous challenge/matchmaking system.
Set up and iterated on the studio's __CI/CD release pipeline__, including a migration from Bitbucket Pipelines to GitHub Actions.

work.name: FRVR
work.summary: **Built gameplay features and live-ops systems** in JavaScript on __a custom PixiJS-based engine__, with deep Facebook Instant Games SDK integration (cloud saves, leaderboards, social contexts, rewarded video).
highlights: **Owned the long-term goals and progression system** for __Basketball FRVR__, the studio’s flagship title — data model, animated UI, reward economy and cross-session cloud sync. The feature drove ==a step change in engagement KPIs==.
**Drove engine 2.0 migration**, low-end device performance work and ad-monetization integrations (LifeStreet, AdMob, Facebook Audience Network).
Shipped daily across web and Facebook Instant to ==an audience in the millions== — A/B tests, canary builds and same-day fixes — localized into 29 languages.

highlights: **Built the core gameplay** for __Color Galaxy__, a 3D io game in the vein of paper.io, and took it to release on Facebook Instant. It was later reworked as Galaxy.io and shipped on Snapchat Games, after I had left.
Developed a range of 2D games in a team of two developers, plus __two 3D games__ for Facebook Instant.
Worked in ==a team of 12 inside a company of 150==, alongside QA, artists, game designers and product owners.
